def count_to(n):
    total = []
    for i in range(1, n):
        total.append(i)
    return total

print(count_to(5))

This was meant to print [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]. What does it ACTUALLY print, exactly, as written?
explanation: range(1, n) stops BEFORE n, so range(1, 5) only produces 1, 2, 3, 4 - the fix is range(1, n + 1) to actually include n itself.
